42e0df71d3.q: How long did it take Urban Betty to reach $1 million in revenue after opening in 2005?
42e0df71d3.a: It took Shelly nine years to make the first million dollars. She describes it as the hardest million you'll ever make, during which she was still working behind the chair five days a week and the only way to get a paycheck was through her own work. Revenue was higher but so were expenses, leaving them roughly equal.

60a3ec84e8.q: What business model change at Urban Betty in 2014 led to 82% growth over three years?
60a3ec84e8.a: In 2014, Urban Betty switched from a hybrid booth rental and commission model to an employee-based system with performance-based leveling. All stylists started at level one and received raises based on performance, not tenure. After implementing these systems, the salon grew 82 percent between 2014 and 2017, and Shelly was able to fully retire from doing hair after three years.

d58b745bdf.q: What financial management system did Shelly Neff implement at Urban Betty in 2020?
d58b745bdf.a: Shelly implemented the Profit First system in 2020 after reading the Profit First book during a two-month closure. The system separates incoming money into specific accounts for payroll, marketing, education, and utilities, allowing visibility into whether expenses exceed budgets and revealing cash leakage. She trained her manager to handle all transfers using this method.

758cd30741.q: How did Urban Betty transition leadership structure as it scaled from 15 to 100 employees?
758cd30741.a: Shelly realized she was trying to run the company as if it were still 15 people when it reached nearly 100. She hired a fractional CFO, brought on Vish software, and hired an HR company for the first time. The leadership team grew to seven people including managers at each location, a CEO, assistant manager, inventory director, and marketing director, all hired from within or promoted from front desk roles.
